decisionsTitle: Four small asks: Girl Zone's address, Mailgun or Gmail per form, an optional email beside the name, the calendar fold
decisionsSection:
**The owner, the evening of 2026-10-14**, four asks (and «YOLO»: the open points are decided here, and said). No migration.

**1. Girl Zone's address is `?tip=girl-zone` (amends §676).** «`?tip=siguranta` trebuie să fie `?tip=girl-zone`». The safety branch's slug is `girl-zone` in both languages (the slug was never localized: one word for the link a club shares or an email carries). `siguranta` stays a **read alias** (`BRANCH_SLUG_ALIASES`): `?tip=siguranta` and `?sent=siguranta` on the wizard answer a redirect to the same query written with `girl-zone` — every other word of it kept (`aliasRedirect`, on a GET only, a plain `redirect`, never a permanent one, so no browser keeps it) — so a link already in a sent email or on paper keeps working. Every address the code builds (`BRANCH_SLUG`: the refusal's, the sent page's, the step-1 choice, the thank-you's) writes the new word; the alias lookup is an own-property test, so `toString` or `__proto__` in the address bar is no branch. Code identifiers do not change (§676 refused it, still): the branch is `safety`, the setting key `feedbackForms`.

**2. «Prin ce trimitem»: the road is the club's choice, per form (amends §676, §678 and §149's «Girl Zone only by Mailgun»).** «Aici trebuie să setăm prin ce trimitem mail (Mailgun sau Gmail)». Each of the four forms has a road, `gmail` — the club's account over SMTP, the one «Scrie-ne» leaves by (§149) — or `mailgun` — the environment's sender. It is a field of the form's entry in the existing `platform_settings` row (`feedbackForms`), so no migration; a row saved before has none and reads as the form's default, which is **exactly what §676 fixed in code: Gmail for «Cum a fost», «O sugestie» and «O reclamație», Mailgun for Girl Zone**. On «Pagini» → «Contact» → «Spune-ne ceva», under each form's recipient, two native radios (`RadioField`, never a toggle; it gained a `disabled`): «Gmail-ul clubului („Scrie-ne”)» and «Mailgun», each with a line saying what it does. The save is audited as a word (`viaChanged`: which form, to which road — never an address). **A road the deployment lacks** (`feedbackRoads`: Gmail where `CONTACT_FORM_MODE` is not `off`, Mailgun where `EMAIL_DELIVERY_MODE` is not `capture`, a laptop and the tests excepted) is greyed with the sentence and a link to its steps in «Sarcini» (the rows `contactForm` and `liveEmail` — the card showed no readiness of its own, so it computes this one); it stays checked when it is what was saved. A greyed radio is never posted, so a save that posts none keeps the road already saved (`keepUnpostedVia`), and the service refuses to *newly* choose a road the deployment lacks, on the form's box. A form whose road is missing is not offered on the site, as the three were not without the SMTP road. **Which road carries a message** follows the form whose reader it reaches (`roadBranch`): a message for the club's mailbox leaves by the road of the form it was written on — a Girl Zone message the sender gave «Clubul» by «O reclamație»'s, whose mailbox it reaches — and a message for the designated person by Girl Zone's own, whatever form it was written on. With the defaults that is §678 to the letter. Screening is by the reader, not the road: a message for the club's mailbox is marked «[posibil spam]» or held back on the Administrator's tick (§310, §744) on either road, a message for her never. Mailgun sends one message per recipient (the allowlist and the allowance count addresses one by one) and counts as sent when any took it. **Girl Zone by Gmail** puts her messages in the club's mailbox and the account's Sent folder, which everybody who reads it sees: the card says so in one line under Girl Zone's radios — «Prin Gmail, mesajul Girl Zone rămâne în căsuța clubului și îl văd cei care o citesc; prin Mailgun ajunge doar la persoana de mai sus» — so her confidentiality is the club's choice. The footer says the road is chosen per form. **The privacy notice's template says so too** (template only; the text in force is untouched): its feedback paragraph no longer promises that her messages never pass through the club's mailbox without saying «unless the club chooses its Gmail for her messages», and says an ordinary message reaches the club's mailbox «through Gmail or Mailgun, as the club chooses». **Not gated by code:** a notice in force that still promises «without passing through the club's mailbox» is false the day the club ticks Gmail for Girl Zone; the card's line and `SETUP.md` say to approve the notice from the new template first, and nothing refuses it — the owner decides whether it should (see the open question).

**3. The optional email beside the name (amends §678).** «Și dacă aleg „nume și prenume” ar trebui să fie și un mail opțional». **It was already there** on the three ordinary forms since §678 («E-mail (opțional)», shown with the name by CSS alone, always present without scripts, dropped server-side from an anonymous post, `Reply-To` by the SMTP road) and on Girl Zone as the way-back line («un email sau un telefon»); what this adds is what the ask needs to be true: the address is validated through the **versioned canonicalizer** (AGENTS.md §10.4; `z.email()` first, then `canonicalizeEmail`, what is kept is the typed address trimmed — capitals and a `+tag` are the person's own), so «Ana <ana@…>», two addresses, a zero-width character or a bare `+tag@gmail.com` are refused on the box with the box's name, kept from the sealed draft; the typed address is the message's `Reply-To` **on both roads** (the adapter gained a per-message `replyTo`, a bare address, never the typed name — which would be a header; Mailgun's `noReplyTo` still outranks it and is what an anonymous or address-less message carries, so nobody is answered at the shared mailbox by default); on Girl Zone's form the way-back line is the `Reply-To` when it is an address and none when it is a telephone. **Nothing is stored:** no table, no outbox row, no audit row, no bucket key (the hourly bucket is the branch's), no log word; the footer's «site-ul nu păstrează niciun mesaj» stays true. **Does the notice in force have to name it first? No** — the named mode itself is gated on `{{feedbackFormsNamed}}` in the notice in force (§678) and exists only while it names it; the email is a box of that mode, and the template's feedback paragraph already said «împreună cu un e-mail sau un telefon, dacă vrei să-ți răspundem». The template now says «(opțional)» and that the email becomes the message's reply address and the platform does not keep it; a notice approved before has the older, still-true sentence, so no new gate.

**4. «Adaugă în calendar» is one pill (amends §767).** «Asta ar trebui să fie collapsed, că nu vedem tot șirul de opțiuni». The five doors stay, in §767's order and words, behind **one small pill** — the share row's own 28-pixel pill with its tap band (`SHARE_PILL_SX`) drawn on the `<summary>` of a native `<details>`, closed on arrival: the calendar glyph, «Adaugă în calendar», a chevron that turns when it opens. No island and no MUI `Menu`: it opens with a click, Enter or Space, and with scripts off. Open, the five pills wrap on one line under it, then the file's note (§674) and the file's address fold (a fold inside the fold), all moved inside so the closed page shows one small control; the share row «Dă mai departe» is unchanged and stays above. The summary's words lost their colon (a caption's colon is not a pill's).

**Refused.** A localized slug for Girl Zone (§676's one-word-both-languages reasoning stands). A permanent redirect for the alias. Renaming the code's `safety` or the setting key. Gating the road by notice in code (see the open question). A second road as a fallback when the chosen one refuses — «Nu am putut trimite acum…» with the text kept, as before; a message that falls to Gmail after Mailgun refuses defeats the choice. A new `Email` box on Girl Zone's form beside the way-back line: two boxes for one purpose, and a telephone is the way back for some.

**Open question for the owner.** Should choosing Gmail for Girl Zone be refused (greyed, like a missing road) until a privacy notice from this release's template is in force in both languages, the way the named mode waits for `{{feedbackFormsNamed}}`? It would take one more marker and one `/admin/tasks` row; decided no here because the club, not a visitor, chooses it, and the card says so.
changelogLine: - **Four small asks** — Girl Zone's address is `?tip=girl-zone` (`siguranta` still opens it), each «Spune-ne ceva» form has a «Prin ce trimitem» choice between the club's Gmail and Mailgun, the optional email beside the name is checked and becomes the reply address on either road, and «Adaugă în calendar» is one small pill that opens the five doors. §NNN.

specsCriteria.text: Girl Zone's form is addressed `?tip=girl-zone` in both languages, in every address the code builds (the choice, a refusal's, the sent page's); `?tip=siguranta` and `?sent=siguranta` answer a redirect to the same query written with `girl-zone`, every other word of it kept, and an unknown word, `toString` or `__proto__` is no branch. Tested in tests/unit/feedback/branches.test.ts and tests/e2e/feedback.spec.ts (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Under each of the four forms on «Pagini» → «Contact» → «Spune-ne ceva», «Prin ce trimitem» is a pair of native radios — «Gmail-ul clubului („Scrie-ne”)» and «Mailgun» — saved in the existing `feedbackForms` setting and audited as a word; the default is Gmail for the three and Mailgun for Girl Zone, so a row saved before reads as it did; a road the deployment lacks is greyed with a link to its steps in «Sarcini», kept when it is what was saved and refused when newly chosen; a form whose road is missing is not offered; a message leaves by the road of the form whose reader it reaches, with the same screening by either road, Mailgun with tracking off and Gmail unchanged; Girl Zone carries a one-line note that Gmail means the club's mailbox readers see the message, and the card's footer says the road is chosen per form. Tested in tests/integration/feedback/submit.test.ts, tests/unit/feedback/branches.test.ts, tests/unit/feedback/feedback-forms-panel.test.ts and tests/e2e/feedback.spec.ts (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

Where a person chooses to give their name, the optional «E-mail (opțional)» box is validated through the versioned canonicalizer (an address it refuses is refused on the box, and kept from the sealed draft), is the message's `Reply-To` by Gmail and by Mailgun — on Girl Zone's form the way-back line when it is an address — and is stored nowhere: no table, no outbox or audit row, no bucket key. The privacy notice's template says the email is optional and becomes the message's reply address; the notice in force need not name it first, the named mode being gated on `{{feedbackFormsNamed}}`. Tested in tests/integration/feedback/submit.test.ts, tests/unit/feedback/branches.test.ts and tests/e2e/feedback.spec.ts (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).

On an event page, «Adaugă în calendar» is one small pill — the share row's 28-pixel pill with its glyph, the words and a chevron — that is the summary of a native fold closed on arrival; open, the five doors (Google Calendar, Apple Calendar, Outlook.com, Outlook for work or school, the `.ics`) wrap on one line under it in the subscription panel's words and order, followed by the file's note and address; it opens by click, Enter or Space and with scripts off, and the share row above is unchanged. Tested in tests/unit/events/share-row-calendars.test.ts and tests/e2e/share-links.spec.ts (2026-10-15, `DECISIONS.md` §NNN).
